method: Each eval run once with the skill and once without (Claude Code subagents, scratch copies of the repositories, act 0.2.97 on Apple Silicon). Graded against the assertions below. One run per configuration: a small sample.

evals.name: setup-x402
evals.prompt: set up local CI for this repo (x402-dotnet) so I stop burning GitHub Actions minutes. I want to be able to run the same checks on my mac before pushing.
assertions: Local config uses act against the existing .github/workflows YAML (no translated second pipeline)
.secrets (or any file holding secrets) is listed in .gitignore
act actually executed at least one CI job (log shows job steps running, not only -n / -l)
Report classifies OIDC/publish/release steps as not runnable locally
Report names the missing secrets (e.g. BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL) without inventing values
No GitHub workflow trigger was changed; cutting GitHub triggers is presented as a user decision with its trade-off

evals.name: sync-after-workflow-edit
evals.fixture: Fixture: a working .actrc/.secrets setup (ubuntu-latest mapping, --container-architecture linux/amd64, --artifact-server-path, NUGET_USER), then a `coverage` job on ubuntu-24.04 using secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN and a `macos-smoke` job on macos-14 added to ci-cd.yml.
evals.prompt: I just added a coverage job and a macos smoke job to TaLibStandard's ci-cd.yml. My local act setup was working before — is it still in sync with the GitHub workflow? fix whatever needs fixing on the local side.
assertions: Detects that ubuntu-24.04 has no image mapping and adds one to .actrc
Detects CODECOV_TOKEN as a missing secret and does not write a fake value into .secrets
Identifies the macos-14 job as GitHub-only (cannot run under act)
Does not modify .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml
Report states the remaining drift (or clean) explicitly
Removes --container-architecture linux/amd64 from .actrc (or justifies keeping it after a native run)
Moves --artifact-server-path out of the project .actrc
Records the CODECOV_TOKEN decision durably (empty value in .secrets) or asks for it explicitly
Flags that the new jobs lack actions/setup-dotnet and proposes the workflow fix without applying it

evals.name: run-pr-workflow
evals.prompt: run the PR workflow of this repo (PipeException) locally and tell me if it would pass on GitHub
assertions: act ran the pull_request event for real (log shows steps executing)
Report gives a per-job pass/fail result
Any failure is classified as real failure vs act limitation vs local config gap
Does not claim a pass based only on a dry run
Gives a clear verdict that counts a red act-limitation-only step (artifact upload) as a pass, naming the step
Notes that ci.yml is generated by Nuke and does not hand-edit it
The decisive act run is native (no linux/amd64 emulation)
